title: TAPAS: Thermal- and Power-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference in Cloud Platforms
problem: LLM inference workloads exhibit fine-grained millisecond-scale phase transitions (prefill vs. decode) with distinct thermal and power profiles, which traditional cloud thermal and power management techniques are too coarse-grained to handle effectively. Cloud co-location of SaaS and IaaS workloads with differing visibility levels further complicates scheduling.
motivation: Rising demand for generative LLM inference in cloud datacenters creates unprecedented thermal and power management challenges because inference phases switch faster than conventional thermal control loops can respond, risking throttling, SLA violations, and accelerator damage.
method: TAPAS is a scheduler that manages AI language model computations on shared cloud computers, tracking how much heat and power each model uses during different inference phases (prefill—processing the prompt—and decode—generating tokens one at a time) at millisecond scale. Instead of running models at full strength, it adjusts three knobs: how to split computation across processors (model parallelism), the size of the model, and the precision of calculations (quantization). These adjustments let it balance four competing goals: speed, temperature, power consumption, and output quality. The scheduler handles multiple customers on the same hardware, using different control strategies depending on whether it can fully monitor and control each workload.
key_novelty: What's new is that TAPAS tracks how heat and power change at millisecond scale during inference (prefill vs. decode phases) and adjusts model size, quantization, and parallelism to simultaneously optimize temperature, power, speed, and quality in shared cloud servers.
contributions: Characterization of fine-grained thermal and power profiles across LLM inference phases at millisecond granularity
TAPAS: a thermal- and power-aware LLM inference scheduler using model configuration parameters as control knobs
Multi-tenant scheduling strategy handling both SaaS and IaaS workloads with different visibility
Analysis of trade-offs between performance, temperature, power, and output quality in LLM inference
